Great Wall of China

万里长城 - One of the World's Greatest Wonders

Overview

The Great Wall of China is one of the most iconic landmarks in the world, stretching over 13,000 miles (21,000 km) across northern China. Built over centuries to protect against invasions, it offers breathtaking views and a glimpse into China's ancient history. The wall winds through mountains, deserts, and grasslands, creating a spectacular sight that has inspired travelers for generations.

Quick Facts

  • Total Length: 13,171 miles (21,196 km)
  • Built: 7th century BC to 1644 AD
  • UNESCO Status: World Heritage Site since 1987
  • Best Time to Visit: April-May or September-October
  • Entrance Fee: ¥35-¥60 depending on section
  • Opening Hours: 7:00 AM - 6:00 PM (varies by season)

🚗 How to Get There - Transportation

From Beijing City Center

By Bus: Take Bus 877 from Deshengmen Bus Station to Badaling (1.5 hours, ¥12). Buses depart every 20 minutes from 6:00 AM to 12:00 PM.

By Train

S2 Train: Depart from Beijing North Railway Station to Badaling Station (1.5 hours, ¥6.5). Trains run daily but schedule varies.

By Private Car/Taxi

Taxi: From downtown Beijing to Badaling (70km, 1.5 hours, ¥300-400 one way). Can be hired for full day tours (¥800-1000).

Tourist Bus

Official Tour Bus: Departs from Qianmen or Beijing Railway Station. Includes guide and entrance ticket (¥150-200 per person).

🗺️ Recommended Tour Routes

Route 1: Badaling Express (Half Day)

Duration: 3-4 hours
Route: Entrance → North Section → Watchtower 8 → South Section → Exit
Difficulty: Easy (cable car available)
Best for: First-time visitors, families with children

Route 2: Mutianyu Complete (Full Day)

Duration: 5-6 hours
Route: Cable car up → Watchtower 14 → Watchtower 20 (highest) → Watchtower 6 → Toboggan down
Difficulty: Moderate
Best for: Photography enthusiasts, moderate hikers

Route 3: Jinshanling to Simatai (Full Day Hike)

Duration: 6-8 hours
Route: Jinshanling East Gate → Watchtower 24 → Simatai West → Simatai East Gate
Difficulty: Challenging (15km hiking)
Best for: Experienced hikers, adventure seekers

Route 4: Sunrise/Sunset Special

Duration: 2-3 hours
Route: Arrive 1 hour before sunrise/sunset → Best viewpoint → Photography session
Difficulty: Easy to Moderate
Best for: Photographers, romantic couples

💡 Essential Travel Tips

  • Best Time: Visit in April-May or September-October for mild weather and fewer crowds
  • Avoid: National holidays (Oct 1-7, May 1-5) when it's extremely crowded
  • What to Bring: Comfortable hiking shoes, water bottle, sunscreen, hat, camera
  • Physical Fitness: Choose your section based on fitness level - Badaling is easiest, Jinshanling is most challenging
  • Cable Car: Available at Badaling and Mutianyu (¥100-120 round trip) - recommended for elderly or those with limited mobility
  • Toboggan: Fun way down at Mutianyu (¥100) - popular with families
  • Photography: Best light is early morning or late afternoon; bring wide-angle lens
  • Restrooms: Available at entrance areas and major watchtowers
  • Food & Water: Bring your own snacks; prices inside are 2-3x higher
  • Safety: Stay on marked paths, don't climb on unrestored sections without guide

📍 Section Comparison

Which Section Should You Visit?

  • Badaling: Most restored, easiest access, most crowded. Best for first-timers and families.
  • Mutianyu: Well-restored, less crowded than Badaling, has toboggan. Best overall experience.
  • Jinshanling: Partially restored, great for hiking, stunning views. Best for photographers and hikers.
  • Simatai: Unrestored, challenging, open for night tours. Best for adventure seekers.
  • Huanghuacheng: Lakeside wall, unique scenery. Best for those seeking something different.
